paper_core_claims.claim: Eff exposes computational effects as typed operation signatures on first-class instances and lets handlers intercept a matching instance-operation while receiving its delimited continuation.
The denotational computation carrier is either a value or an operation with parameter and continuation; handler semantics rewrites matching operations and forwards unmatched ones.
Top-level resources attach mutable default behavior to instances, enabling reference-like state and built-in real-world I/O when no enclosing handler consumes the operation.
Handlers can discard, resume once or resume multiple times, supporting exceptions, nondeterminism, backtracking, search, probability and cooperative scheduling patterns.
Eff's prototype extends the paper core with Hindley-Milner inference and desugaring into an interpreter whose evaluation structure follows the denotational presentation.

function_concept_used_by_paper: The central callable unit is split between ordinary functions and effectful computations. A computation may return a value or emit an instance-qualified operation together with a delimited continuation; a handler is a first-class computation transformer from handled input values to output computations. This is a programming-language semantic model, not a registry of autonomous business functions.
specification_language: Effect declarations specify finite operation names and parameter/result types; handler clauses specify behavior for selected instance-operation pairs plus value/finally cases. Ordinary function and handler types state value domains but do not record which effects a computation may perform. There are no pre/postconditions, authority policies, resource budgets, compatibility constraints or effect rows.

representation_or_carrier.syntax: Expressions, computations, effect signatures, fresh instances, operations, handlers and optional resources.
representation_or_carrier.semantic_result: A recursively defined result domain containing either a returned value or an operation request with parameter and continuation.
representation_or_carrier.runtime: Closures, first-class effect instances, handler values, operation nodes, multi-shot host-language continuations and resource state cells in the prototype interpreter.
representation_or_carrier.boundary: The model is for an experimental language and does not package a portable, signed or capability-governed Function OS artifact.

compiler_or_generator.front_end: The prototype parses OCaml-like concrete syntax, infers polymorphic value types and desugars mixed expressions/computations into the core separation.
compiler_or_generator.ordering: When multiple computations are hoisted from an expression, simultaneous bindings leave ordering conceptually open; the prototype executes source order and may warn.
compiler_or_generator.classification: This is a parser/desugarer/type-inference front end feeding an interpreter, not a semantics-preserving optimizing compiler, verified code generator or automatic function synthesizer.
compiler_or_generator.effect_boundary: Because types omit effect information, the front end cannot statically certify purity, harmless reordering or all resource restrictions.

interpreter_or_runtime: Evaluation produces a value or an operation node. A handler recursively processes the result, applies a matching clause with a re-entering continuation, or forwards an unmatched operation outward. At top level, a resource operation reads and replaces instance state and resumes; an unhandled operation or a resource clause that itself emits an operation causes a runtime error. The historical OCaml interpreter realizes this architecture.
state_or_effect_model: Effectful computation is explicit at the semantic level through instance-qualified operations and delimited continuations. Handlers may reinterpret or eliminate operations; resources provide mutable top-level state/default behavior and built-ins connect to I/O. State, exceptions, transactions, nondeterminism, probability and cooperative scheduling are expressible patterns. There is no static effect set on ordinary types, permission/authority model, distributed transaction semantics, idempotence, compensation protocol, concurrency isolation or safety sandbox.
composition_rule: Handlers compose by lexical nesting over the recursive result carrier: the nearest matching instance-operation clause handles and may invoke the delimited continuation zero, one or multiple times, while unmatched operations propagate outward. Composition is order-sensitive and not commutative; the paper's backtracking and probability/state examples explicitly show that handler scope and expression sequencing can change or invalidate results.

equivalence_notions.support: The paper assigns compositional domains and interpretation functions to core types, computations, handlers and resources.
equivalence_notions.boundary: It states no soundness, adequacy, contextual-equivalence or mechanized theorem connecting the model to every prototype behavior.

equivalence_notions.support: Matching operations are replaced by clause computations and unmatched operations are re-emitted with transformed continuations.
equivalence_notions.boundary: This does not make differently ordered/nested handler programs equivalent.

equivalence_notions.support: The repository includes executable examples and output-diff regression fixtures.
equivalence_notions.boundary: Example outputs are finite regression observations, not semantic equivalence, proof or broad empirical validation.

validation_regime.paper: Worked programs exercise canonical and unusual effect patterns, and the formal sections provide a compositional denotational account of the core language.
validation_regime.implementation: The paper-era repository contains 26 test programs with 26 expected-output fixtures and a script that runs the interpreter then diffs actual against expected output.
validation_regime.static_checking: The prototype implements Hindley-Milner value typing, but effect behavior is deliberately absent from standard types.
validation_regime.not_run: The historical code could not be built in this environment because the required OCaml toolchain is absent.
validation_regime.missing: No theorem/proof section, mechanized semantics, property-based suite, coverage report, benchmark, performance study, user study, portability matrix, security analysis or immutable release receipt is provided.

uncertainty_model: The language can represent nondeterministic and probabilistic choices through handlers, including enumerated distributions, but it does not model epistemic/predictive uncertainty about a function or handler. There is no confidence calibration, error bar, risk bound, abstention, fallback-selection policy or uncertainty attached to effect routing. Multi-shot continuation behavior is programmer-defined control, not calibrated uncertainty.
lifecycle_and_provenance: A governed Eff/Function OS artifact would pin language/interpreter commit, compiler and OCaml versions, effect/handler interfaces, resource behavior, module hashes, declared ordering, test receipts and compatibility/security policy. The official repository supplies history and BSD-2-Clause code; commit df3d790 explicitly merged paper examples one day after arXiv submission, while a later v3.0 tag retrospectively marks a paper-like stable version. Neither is a publication-time signed release or lifecycle registry, and the current project describes itself as experimental rather than production-ready.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Operation signatures and handler clauses specify typed interfaces and behavior, but ordinary types omit performed effects and there are no contracts, permissions or nonfunctional constraints.

N2_Representation.reason: The paper gives explicit syntax and semantic carriers for effectful computations, instances, handlers, operations, continuations and resources.

N3_Compiler.reason: Parsing, type inference and desugaring are concrete front-end transformations, but execution remains interpretive and effect/order preservation is not formally certified.

N4_Artifact.reason: Historical source programs, interpreter code, examples and regression fixtures are concrete executable artifacts, bounded by missing immutable publication release and unavailable runtime execution here.

N5_Interpreter.reason: The evaluator concretely realizes value/operation results, handler interception/forwarding and top-level resources.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Operation/continuation chains expose a conceptual execution structure, but no durable trace schema, log, causal receipt or deterministic replay protocol is defined.

N7_Validator.reason: Value typing and output-diff regressions validate bounded properties, while effects/order/resource safety remain incompletely checked and tests were not run in this review.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Lexically nested handlers route instance-qualified operations, transform matching requests and forward the rest; ordering is explicit and semantically consequential.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: The paper defines no versioned effect/function capability registry, promotion state, compatibility matrix, monitoring or retirement workflow.

GAP-015.reason: Typed operation signatures and handler clauses are useful specifications, but missing effect rows/contracts/authority constraints leave the broader gap open.

GAP-016.reason: Instance-qualified routing, lexical handler nesting, forwarding and multi-shot continuation use provide a concrete order-sensitive composition algebra.

GAP-017.reason: Denotational semantics and regression fixtures give meaning and finite checks, but no mechanized correspondence, semantic-equivalence validator or adequacy theorem is supplied.

GAP-018.reason: Operations, handlers, resource state, I/O, exceptions and transactional/state examples directly model effects and their interpretation, within the stated runtime/static limits.

GAP-019.reason: Source history and paper-linked commits support provenance, but no immutable artifact receipt, compatibility registry or lifecycle governance exists.

GAP-020.reason: Nondeterministic/probabilistic control is expressible, but there is no calibrated epistemic uncertainty, confidence, risk, abstention or fallback framework.

source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED applies to the bounded semantic and architectural claim: Eff provides typed algebraic operation signatures, first-class instances and handlers, a value-or-operation-plus-continuation semantics, nested operation routing and a concrete interpreter with paper-linked artifacts. It does not confirm the old atlas bibliography, whose sole-author/JFP/Cambridge DOI record is wrong for this source. 'Seamless' combination is narrowed to expressibility and modular syntax: the paper itself demonstrates order- and scope-sensitive failures, warns about arbitrary sequencing and says an effect system is future work. The denotational development is formalization, not a claimed proof of prototype correctness.
confirmed_projection: The paper confirms a strong Function OS pattern for N2/N5/N8 and GAP-016/GAP-018: represent an invocation as either a value or a typed operation request carrying its continuation; route by stable instance plus operation identity; let local handlers transform known requests and forward unknown ones; and make nesting/order part of the explicit composition contract. Its failures show why a production Function OS additionally needs static effect/authority specifications, ordering checks, durable traces, lifecycle provenance and runtime rollback/fallback boundaries.
projection_boundary: This projection is based on the exact 25-page arXiv v1 bytes, all rendered pages, complete text, official arXiv/Crossref metadata and the relevant official repository history/source/examples/tests. The historical implementation was not built or executed because its toolchain is absent. This model review is not a proof, formal verification, code reproduction, independent empirical validation, security audit or validation of ignition.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not support the old atlas's sole-author, Journal of Functional Programming or DOI 10.1017/S0956796815000120 binding.
It does not provide an effect system that statically records performed effects or proves reordering harmless.
It does not show that handler composition is commutative, order-independent or automatically understandable; several examples show the opposite.

It does not provide general ACID transactions, distributed commit, compensation or external-system rollback; its transaction example temporarily handles one reference and commits only on a returned value.
It does not allow resource clauses to emit further operations; doing so is a runtime error in the presented model.
It does not type every expressible control example; the yin-yang self-application requires disabling the type checker.
It does not prove soundness, adequacy, contextual equivalence or implementation correspondence.
It does not benchmark performance, scalability or operational reliability.
It does not define permissions, authority, sandboxing, safety policy, durable tracing or a versioned capability registry.
The repository artifacts and expected outputs do not by themselves reproduce or independently validate every paper claim.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The paper's formal core is monomorphic, while the prototype adds polymorphic inference and syntactic desugaring outside that core presentation.
Standard types do not contain computational-effect information; effect-system design is explicitly future work.
Simultaneous computation ordering is not semantically neutral, and the prototype warns rather than rejecting ambiguous sequencing.
Handler nesting and state scope can make backtracking/probability examples correct or wrong.
Unhandled operations and invalid resource results are runtime failures.
Resources cannot safely evaluate computations that trigger operations in the presented interpreter.
Multi-shot continuations can duplicate work and state interaction; no resource-cost or linearity discipline is given.
Continuations are acknowledged as non-algebraic even though handlers can encode useful delimited-control patterns.
The historical test suite checks expected outputs but supplies no coverage, property, concurrency, security or platform guarantees.
The implementation remains an experimental research language and the paper leaves program reasoning and effect analysis for future work.

prior_provisional_comparison.old_template: Function with explicit effect tracking via handler algebra; algebraic effect signature; effect handler compiler/runtime; deterministic with nondeterminism effects; effect observation equivalence; effect log; language version.
prior_provisional_comparison.accepted_after_full_review: Typed effect signatures, first-class instances/handlers, order-sensitive nested composition, explicit operation-plus-continuation semantics and a prototype interpreter are directly supported.
prior_provisional_comparison.corrected_after_full_review: The paper is by Bauer and Pretnar in JLAMP with DOI 10.1016/j.jlamp.2014.02.001. Ordinary types do not explicitly track performed effects; the artifact is an interpreter rather than an effect-handler compiler; probabilistic/nondeterministic handlers do not make the system deterministic; no effect-observation equivalence theorem or effect-log trace is supplied; and repository history is not a governed language-version registry.
